LLM_description:
Situation:
The brigade is conducting sustained operations across a contested river valley and adjacent high ground. Ground lines of communication are constrained by intermittent indirect fire, IED activity, and limited engineer support for route clearance. Air resupply is restricted due to weather and air defense threats, making ground convoys the primary distribution method. Supply Depot Bravo and Depot Sierra hold rations, ammunition, and medical supplies for onward movement to multiple forward units, including the 3rd Infantry Battalion, Artillery Battery Kilo, and Engineer Company Lima.

Mission:
Deliver required supplies to all supported units throughout the planning window while minimizing total operational cost. Cost elements include transport, shortage penalties for authorized shortfalls, vehicle deployment, and fixed route security risk costs. Ensure units maintain combat effectiveness and readiness with risk acceptable to command.

Execution/Concept:
- Distribution will be planned by depot-to-unit, by supply type, for each day, within depot stock constraints. Units will receive their scheduled demands; authorized shortfalls may be accepted when risk or capacity necessitates, incurring penalty costs.
- Convoys will be task-organized and loaded against vehicle capacity; shipments on a route cannot exceed the aggregate carrying capacity of the vehicles assigned. Supply volume factors will determine load mix.
- Routes must be explicitly activated before movement. Vehicles can only use active routes. Activating a route on a given day incurs a fixed Risk Cost representing security overhead (escort teams, route clearance, overwatch, and QRF posture), regardless of how many vehicles are sent on that route.
- Total vehicles available for the day are limited. Vehicle allocation across routes will be balanced to meet priority demands while minimizing transport cost and exposure.
- Movement Control Team will synchronize convoy timings with ISR and fires to mitigate exposure on the valley corridors. Engineer and EOD teams will be scheduled to support only activated routes. Consolidation of loads and avoidance of splitting shipments across multiple routes will reduce repeated payment of fixed risk costs.
- Priority of support will be given to units in contact and those with mission-critical ammunition and medical requirements. Lower-risk corridors will be favored; high-risk routes will be used only when necessary and with consolidated movements to optimize security overhead.
- End state: All supported units sustain operations with acceptable risk; the fleet remains within limits; only essential routes are activated; total operational cost is minimized.
